title: DART: Domain-Agnostic Residual Transfer for Generalist Anomaly Detection
abstract: arXiv:2611.08271v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Generalist Anomaly Detection (GAD) aims to detect anomalies in unseen domains using only a few reference samples. Recent normal-abnormal guided methods improve this setting by exploiting abnormal references, but their residuals often mix transferable anomaly cues with domain-specific appearance factors such as texture, geometry, and acquisition conditions. This residual domain entanglement limits cross-domain transfer and may produce spurious activations on novel domains. We propose DART, a plug-in framework for normal-abnormal guided GAD that learns to separate residuals into anomaly-relevant and domain-specific components. DART combines a Residual Disentanglement Module, which preserves anomaly-discriminative information while suppressing domain information, with Cross-Domain Meta-Training, which forms episodes across source domains to make the separation effective. translated_title: DART：面向通用异常检测的领域无关残差迁移
translated_abstract: 通用异常检测（GAD）旨在仅使用少量参考样本来检测未见领域中的异常。近期的正常-异常引导方法通过利用异常参考样本改进了这一设置，但其残差往往将可迁移的异常线索与领域特定的外观因素（如纹理、几何形状和采集条件）混杂在一起。这种残差的领域纠缠限制了跨领域迁移，并可能在新的领域上产生虚假激活。我们提出DART，这是一个面向正常-异常引导GAD的即插即用框架，它学习将残差分离为异常相关成分和领域特定成分。DART将残差解耦模块（在保留异常判别信息的同时抑制领域信息）与跨领域元训练（在源域之间构建训练片段以使这种分离有效）相结合。该方法与架构无关，可以插入到残差特征提取之间……
tldr: DART提出了一种即插即用框架，通过残差解耦模块与跨领域元训练，将正常-异常参考残差分离为异常相关成分与领域特定成分，从而提升通用异常检测的跨域迁移能力。
en_tdlr: DART is a plug-in framework that combines a Residual Disentanglement Module with Cross-Domain Meta-Training to separate residuals into anomaly-relevant and domain-specific components, improving cross-domain transfer for generalist anomaly detection.
